newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Russia confident Moldova will not join NATO.
newsitem.headline: Russia confident Moldova will not join NATO.

text.p: A Russian official visiting Moldova shortly after NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, said on Wednesday he was confident the former Soviet republic would not join the Western alliance.

Yuri Baturin, a senior defence official, held talks in the capital Chisinau two days after Solana visited Moldova to discuss and explain NATO's plans to take in new members from eastern and central Europe. Moscow opposes those plans.

"Historical ties between Russia and Moldova are so strong that it is difficult to say Moldova will move in the direction of NATO," Baturin, secretary of Russia's advisory Defence Council, told reporters.

NATO is expected to issue formal membership invitations in July to Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic. Russia has made clear it would oppose any moves to invite former Soviet republics to join the alliance.
Baturin's talks included discussion of Russia's 6,000 troops from Moldova's breakaway Dnestr region and prospects for settling political conflict there.
He said immediately after arriving in Moldova on Tuesday that Russia would pull the troops out only when the Dnestr conflict is resolved.
Russia has had troops in Dnestr since clashes erupted over its independence moves in 1992, although Chisinau and Moscow signed an agreement in 1994 for the troops to be withdrawn within three years.
"Prospects for the settlement are good, and the pace of withdrawal will depend on the outcome of talks between Moldova and Dnestr," Baturin said.
That amounted to a rebuffal to Solana, who said during his visit to Moldova that the agreement to remove the troops within three years should stand.
Baturin said Russia planned to reduce the number of troops in Dnestr, but declined to give details.
Moldova's President Petru Lucinschi has said Russian troops will gradually be reduced to 2,000 servicemen.
